title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims 'The grafted model achieves FID=2.77, substantially outperforming all baseline models regardless of depth or parameter count. Notably, our grafted model surpasses even the original DiT-XL/2 (FID=2.27)...'. But Table 6 reports Grafting FID=2.77 vs DiT-XL/2 FID=2.27. Since lower FID is better, the grafted model is measurably WORSE than the original DiT-XL/2 by the paper's own numbers. The claim that 2.77 'surpasses' 2.27 is a direct contradiction of the reported results in Table 6.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.4 Locality Analysis (text) vs Figure 2 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3.4 text states 'for k=32, all 28 layers exhibit L_k > 0.7, with 22 layers exceeding 0.85'. The Figure 2 caption states 'At k=32, 15 out of 28 layers exhibit values exceeding 0.5'. If 22 of 28 layers exceed 0.85, then by monotonicity 22 layers necessarily exceed 0.5, directly contradicting the caption's claim that only 15 layers exceed 0.5. The two statements in the same section are mutually exclusive.

The Abstract claims 'all tested hybrid designs achieve excellent quality (FID: 2.15–2.38 vs. 2.27 for DiT-XL/2)'. However, the body (Result I, Section 4) reports FID 'between 2.38 and 2.64', and the Conclusion repeats 'competitive quality (FID 2.38–2.64 vs. 2.27 baseline)'. Moreover, no FID value of 2.15 appears anywhere in the paper's tables; the best hybrid value in Table 4 is 2.37 (r=6 at 75%). The Abstract's lower bound of 2.15 is unsupported and inconsistent with the body text.

The Abstract claims grafting 'consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios and operator types'. The body (Section 4.2) explicitly states the opposite for full replacement: 'At 100% replacement, performance sharply degrades (all FIDs > 75)' (baseline FID = 2.27). Full MHA replacement yields FID > 75 in Table 4, which does not outperform the 2.27 baseline. The Abstract overstates the results reported in the main text.

Section 3.3 text states 'using just 10% of the training data (128k samples), we achieve an FID of 2.53 vs. 2.27 for the baseline' for full MHA self-grafting. Table 2 reports MHA Full Self-grafting at 10.0% data with FID = 2.49 (IS 287.81), and MLP at 10.0% with FID = 2.54. The text's 2.53 matches neither (2.49 for MHA, 2.54 for MLP). Figure 4(a) also lists full self-grafting at 10% data as 2.49, confirming the text's 2.53 is inconsistent with the tables.

The Abstract, Section 5, and Conclusion claim a '1.43x speedup' (43%) for the grafted PixArt-Sigma model. Table 5 reports latency 148.32 ms (1.59x) for the 50% Hyena-X model and 194.95 ms (1.21x) for the 29% model. No row in Table 5 yields 1.43x. The text describes the grafted model as the 50% configuration (GenEval 47.78, layers 8,10,12,14,16,18,20-27 = 14/28 layers), whose speedup is 1.59x. The claimed 1.43x appears nowhere in the reported data.

Figure 1(c) reports FIDs for hybrid designs (Hyena-Y 2.61, SWA 2.62, Mamba-2 2.55, Hyena-X 2.64, r=3 2.53, r=6 2.38). These match the 20%-data values in Figure 4(a)/Fig C.1 for the MHA variants (Hyena-X 2.61, Hyena-Y 2.61, SWA 2.62, Mamba-2 2.55), but Table 4 - the main results table using 10% data - reports Hyena-X 50% FID 2.74, Hyena-Y 2.72, SWA 2.67, Mamba-2 2.65. The MLP values (r=3 2.53, r=6 2.38) match Table 4's 10%-data rows. The headline figure mixes 20%-data and 10%-data results without disclosure, inconsistent with Table 4.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5 text vs Figure 4 (reference and thresholds)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 5 text states Hyena-X 'achieving FID 2.61 with 20% data (see Fig. 4(b))', but the 20%-data values appear in Fig. 4(a) (data-scaling ablation), while Fig. 4(b) is the layer-selection heuristic ablation. Additionally, degradation at full replacement is described inconsistently across the paper: text says 'all FIDs > 75' (Section 4.2), Fig 4(b) reports 'FID > 140', and the Table 4 caption defines the 'x' marker as 'FID > 50'. These three thresholds do not agree.

summary: The paper 'Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting' (NeurIPS 2025 submission, cs.LG) was verified in exhaustive mode with lenient strictness. The core technical content - the diffusion objective (Eq. 1), the regression-based activation-distillation objective (Eq. 2), the band-k locality metric (Eq. 3), the Hyena operator equations (Appendix G), and the MHA FLOP arithmetic (Appendix H: 6LD^2 + 2LD^2 = 8LD^2, 2L^2D + HL^2) - is mathematically sound; no provable algebraic errors were found. However, the paper contains multiple high-confidence internal inconsistencies between its claims and its own reported data: (1) the case study claims the grafted 14-layer model (FID 2.77) surpasses DiT-XL/2 (FID 2.27), which is contradicted by Table 6 (lower FID is better); (2) the locality analysis text ('all 28 layers L_k > 0.7, 22 exceeding 0.85') contradicts the Figure 2 caption ('15 out of 28 layers exceed 0.5'); (3) the Abstract's hybrid FID range 2.15-2.38 is unsupported (no such value appears anywhere; body/conclusion report 2.38-2.64); (4) the Abstract claims grafting 'consistently outperforms the baseline across all replacement ratios' while the body reports full-replacement FIDs > 75; (5) the MHA full self-grafting FID is reported as 2.53 in the text but 2.49 in Table 2; (6) the PixArt-Sigma speedup is claimed as 1.43x but Table 5 reports 1.59x for the described 50% model; (7) Figure 1(c) mixes 20%- and 10%-data FIDs without disclosure relative to Table 4; (8) inconsistent degradation thresholds (FID > 50 / > 75 / > 140) and a wrong figure reference (Fig. 4(b) vs 4(a)). These are internal-consistency defects in reported numbers and claims that warrant correction before publication.
